text:
American marine biologist Zachary Wallace joined an expedition to the Sargasso Sea to study giant squids. While there, sonar detected a signal the military had nicknamed the Bloop. As the sounds closed in, the three passengers aboard the submarine—Zachary, Hank, and the pilot—watched in horror as a giant squid was torn apart by several unidentified creatures. The submarine’s acrylic bubble sustained severe damage, and the three scrambled to ascend. Before reaching the research boat, the bubble ruptured. The Atlantic flooded in, killing the pilot and drowning Wallace as he shoved Hank toward safety. Miraculously, Wallace survived.

Back in South Florida, he returned to take his position at Florida Atlantic University. But he soon learned that David, a colleague, blamed him for the sub’s destruction and the pilot’s death. Fired, Zachary spiraled, spending every cent on drinks and nightclubs. Weeks later, he received word that his biological father, Angus Wallace, was on trial for murder. Angus lived in a village on the shores of Loch Ness, Scotland. Zachary had not seen him since his mother divorced him and returned to the U.S. seventeen years earlier.

Still, he agreed to visit when his half-brother insisted he was needed. He reconnected with old friends and prepared to help his father. But the trial complicated everything. Angus maintained his innocence, insisting he had seen the victim attacked by the Loch Ness Monster. The British tabloids exploded. Boats and crews flocked to the loch, hunting for Nessie.

Desperate to rebuild his academic reputation, Zachary now had to uncover the truth—among old friends, his family, the enigmatic Black Knights, a secret branch of the Knights Templar, and deeper, hidden layers of the past.

Jenny Humphrey has attended many wild parties at Waverly Academy, but none as intense as the one at Miller farm, where the antique red barn burned down. When Dean Marymount announces that someone will be expelled for the arson, panic spreads. Everyone becomes a suspect. Jenny worries about Julian, her new crush, whose silver-engraved Zippo was found at the scene. Callie fears she and Easy will both be kicked out, since they were in the barn when the fire started. Tinsley, who organized the event, knows she’ll be blamed and decides to shift responsibility onto Jenny.

Tinsley’s plan succeeds at first. Julian and Jenny grow closer, but their connection shatters when Jenny learns Julian only approached her because he was secretly involved with Tinsley. Trust breaks down. Easy becomes suspicious of Callie after her remarks about Jenny starting the fire. Meanwhile, Kara and Brett’s relationship becomes public. Brett realizes he still loves Jeremiah, and after a shift in dynamics, Kara begins dating Heath.

Tinsley’s scheme backfires. Easy discovers Callie was part of the plot to frame Jenny. He tries to intervene, but Callie and Easy’s relationship ends. Easy is repelled by Callie’s role in the setup, and Jenny remains angry at Julian for lying to her. The situation resolves when Easy claims he paid off Old Lady Miller to prevent the case from moving forward. She confirms her cows, not Jenny, caused the fire. Jenny is cleared.

Later, Jenny admits she set the barn on fire—not to harm anyone, but because she could no longer endure the accusations, hostile stares, and rumors. She is expelled. But she is eventually readmitted to Waverly.

text:
American marine biologist Zachary Wallace joined an expedition into the Sargasso Sea to document giant squids. During the dive, sonar detected a signal previously designated as the Bloop. As the sound intensified, the three aboard the submarine—Zachary, Hank, and the pilot—observed a giant squid torn apart by multiple unidentified predators. The submarine’s acrylic bubble sustained catastrophic damage. In the rush to ascend, the three scrambled toward the surface. Before reaching the research vessel, the bubble ruptured, flooding the cabin. The pilot died instantly, and Wallace drowned briefly before being pulled to safety by Hank. Miraculously, he survived.

Returning to South Florida, Wallace assumed a position at Florida Atlantic University. There, he learned that David, a colleague and former confidant, held him responsible for the sub’s destruction and the pilot’s death. Dismissed from the university, Wallace sank into despair, exhausting his savings on alcohol and nightlife.

Weeks later, he received news: his biological father, Angus Wallace, was on trial for murder. Angus lived in a remote village on the shores of Loch Ness, Scotland. Zachary had not seen him since his mother’s divorce, which occurred seventeen years earlier when she returned to the U.S. Though reluctant, he agreed to travel to Scotland upon learning his half-brother needed him at the trial.

He reconnected with old friends in South Florida and began preparing for the journey. But the situation grew complicated when Angus took the stand and denied the murder. He claimed to have seen the victim attacked by the Loch Ness Monster. The announcement triggered media frenzy. British tabloids seized the story, and Loch Ness quickly filled with boats, crews, and tourists hunting for evidence.

With his academic career in ruins, Zachary resolved to uncover the truth. He would investigate his father’s testimony, the network of old friends, the secretive Black Knights—a clandestine offshoot of the Knights Templar—and long-buried family secrets. His mission was not just to clear his father’s name, but to reclaim his own.

text: Aging is linked to an increased risk of falls, with impaired ability to recover balance following postural perturbations serving as a key contributing factor. This deficit is likely attributable to age-related declines in lower limb strength. The present study examined how age-related strength loss affects non-stepping balance recovery after a perturbation while standing, without restricting movement to the ankle, as in prior work. Two experiments were performed. In the first, five young adults (20–30 years) and six community-dwelling older adults (70–80 years) recovered balance without stepping from a backward displacement of the support surface. Balance recovery capacity was measured as the maximum backward platform displacement tolerated without stepping. The older group achieved a maximal displacement 27% smaller than the young group (11.8 ± 2.1 cm vs. 16.2 ± 2.6 cm). In the second experiment, forward dynamic simulations using a two-segment, rigid-body model explored the impact of altering strength in hip extensors/flexors and ankle plantar flexors/dorsiflexors, incorporating typical age-related strength reductions. The model predicted reduced maximal platform displacements exclusively when plantar flexion and hip flexion strength were diminished. These results corroborate prior evidence of age-related decline in balance recovery, and highlight a critical role for plantar flexor strength in maintaining postural stability during perturbations.

text: Going After Cacciato, like many stories exploring psychological trauma, holds deliberate ambiguities about the sequence and nature of events, requiring readers to look past the narrator’s surface-level language. The book’s chronology is nonlinear for much of its length. According to O'Brien, the central idea is that serving a standard tour in Vietnam means constant walking. If all that walking were straightened into one line, it would reach Paris—where Cacciato is headed. Cacciato is consistently portrayed as self-sufficient and content. He is the one being pursued throughout the novel’s imagined narrative. The final pages present a contrast between two statements—one by Sarkin Aung Wan, the other by Paul Berlin—highlighting a shift from the early American ideal of independence and happiness (as seen in Emerson and Thoreau) to the modern reality of societal obligations that pressure individuals into compliance, even complicity in violence. Cacciato marches to a different rhythm, living freely and happily in a carefree, almost oblivious way. Though his actions sometimes suggest he lacks intelligence or depth, he remains untroubled by the war’s larger questions. Paul Berlin, the novel’s central figure, is a soldier worn down by frustration. Throughout the story, he fixates on every small detail, whether from memory or from the imagined pursuit. In the chapter titled "Tunneling Toward Paris," the characters escape the endless tunnels by "falling out" just as they fell in—an allusion to Alice in Wonderland that reveals the story’s surreal nature. This surrealism appears earlier, too, when Cacciato is shown flying off a mountain.

The Eastern Conference defeated the Western Conference in the 2008 National Basketball Association All-Star Game, held Sunday at the New Orleans Arena in New Orleans, Louisiana. The final score was 134-128. The West trailed by 13 points at the start of the fourth quarter, but mounted a comeback fueled by New Orleans point guard Chris Paul, who recorded seven assists in the final period. With 2:48 left, Brandon Roy scored a layup off a Paul pass, giving the West a 122-119 lead—their largest of the game.

The East responded with back-to-back three-pointers from Ray Allen. Paul then tied the game with a three-pointer of his own. But the East regained the lead and won the game with a sequence of finishes: layups from Dwyane Wade and Allen, followed by a driving dunk from LeBron James. With 8.7 seconds remaining, Roy hit a three-pointer to cut the deficit to three points. Ray Allen then sealed the victory with three free throws.

While the All-Star Game remains the centerpiece of the weekend’s events, the festivities also featured several other competitions highlighting the league’s top talent. The Sophomores defeated the Rookies 136-109 in the Rookie Challenge, showcasing the best young players in the league. Cleveland Cavaliers guard Daniel Gibson was named MVP, scoring all 33 of his points from three-pointers. He broke Kyle Korver’s 2005 record of seven three-pointers in a single game. This marked the sixth consecutive victory for the Sophomores.

Team San Antonio won the Three-Point Shootout, a contest featuring current and former NBA stars and WNBA players. The team, composed of Spurs forward Tim Duncan, former Spurs center David Robinson, and Silver Stars guard Becky Hammon, defeated Team Chicago in the final round on a halfcourt shot by Duncan.

Deron Williams won the PlayStation Skills Challenge with a record time of 25.5 seconds in the final. His performance outpaced Chris Paul, who finished in 31.2 seconds. Dwyane Wade, who had won the past two years, failed to advance past the first round, clocking in at 53.9 seconds. Jason Kidd was also eliminated in the first round, finishing in 39.7 seconds.

Toronto Raptors guard Jason Kapono claimed his second consecutive Three-Point Shootout title, becoming the first back-to-back winner since Peja Stojakovic in 2002 and 2003. Kapono matched the record of 25 points in the final round, set by Mark Price and Craig Hodges in 1986. Daniel Gibson scored 17 points in the final round, and Dirk Nowitzki, the 2006 champion, scored 14. Stojakovic, Richard Hamilton, and Steve Nash were eliminated in the first round.

A rare white marble statue with facial features resembling Alexander the Great has been uncovered in Egypt, according to Zahi Hawass, Egypt’s leading archaeologist and Secretary General of the Supreme Council of Antiquities. The find was made during a Greek-led excavation in Alexandria, where Calliope Papacosta was in charge. The discovery adds to growing evidence of Hellenistic influence in the region. Satellite imaging has also helped identify numerous unexcavated archaeological sites across Egypt, with the National Authority for Remote Sensing, Space Sciences (NARRS) and Mubarak City for Scientific Research (MuCSAT) combining satellite data, aerial photography, and ground laser scanning to pinpoint 132 potential locations. Among them are sites near Lake Qarun in the Faiyum region and in Habu city. 

The Egyptian Ministry of Tourism is now dispatching archaeologists to areas ahead of construction projects to protect valuable historical remains. At the Faiyum site, artifacts from multiple eras have surfaced, including a leather-stitching awl, fishing gear, weapons, jewelry, pottery, coins, sawfish remains, whale fossils, and a 3150 BC stone block depicting one of two kings named Scorpion. These findings highlight the region’s long and layered human history.

Meanwhile, in Iran, the country’s three salt mummies—discovered in the Chehrabad Salt Mine in 1993—will be relocated to a high-tech vacuum chamber display in Zanjan. The mummies, known as Salt Men, date from the Parthian period (237 BCE–224 CE) and the Sassanid era (224–651 CE). The move aims to improve their preservation through controlled environmental conditions. Egypt’s culture minister, Farouk Hosni, continues to support archaeological research and has enforced laws to prevent illegal digging on confirmed sites containing historical monuments.

text:
In the late 18th century, amid the shifting currents of empire and culture, a quiet but profound transformation unfolded in India’s Deccan. Among British officials stationed in Hyderabad, a pattern emerged: one in three British men living there married Indian women, a testament not to policy but to personal choice, intimacy, and a complex, often overlooked, intercultural exchange. At the center of this world stands Captain James Achilles Kirkpatrick, East India Company resident of Hyderabad, whose life became a living paradox—loyal to his employers, yet deeply committed to the customs and faith of the people he was sent to supervise. His marriage to Khair-un-Nissa, a Hyderabadi noblewoman of Persian lineage, was not merely a personal union but a political and spiritual act. He converted to Islam, adopting the name Abdullah Khan, and lived openly as a Muslim, his loyalty to the Nizam of Hyderabad as much a function of diplomacy as of conviction. His story, as told in White Mughals, reflects a moment when British and Indian lives intertwined in ways that defied later imperial narratives.

The book, grounded in letters, memoirs, and encrypted dispatches, reconstructs a world where boundaries between faiths were less rigid than often assumed. It examines the fluidity between Christianity and Islam in pre-modern India, highlighting pockets of mutual respect and intellectual exchange. Yet it also traces the slow erosion of such openness. After the rise of Evangelical Christianity within Britain’s ruling class, a new hostility emerged—not only toward mixed unions but toward the children born of them, who were increasingly dismissed as racially impure. This shift, carefully documented by historian William Dalrymple, marks a turning point in how empire understood identity.

Kirkpatrick’s death leaves behind a legacy shaped by love and loss. The final chapter of the narrative is not one of triumph, but of quiet endurance. His two children, sent to England, carry forward a different kind of connection. The daughter, Kitty, grows into a woman of quiet intellect and grace, forming a close friendship with Thomas Carlyle. Years later, she renews correspondence with her grandmother in Hyderabad, rekindling a bond severed by distance and empire. The story, though rooted in tragedy, closes not in silence, but in a fragile, enduring thread of memory and kinship.

<source>
 The book is a work of social history about the warm relations that existed between the British and some Indians in the 18th and early 19th century, when one in three British men in India was married to an Indian woman. It documents the interracial liaisons between British officers, such as Major-General Charles Stuart, and Indian women, and the geopolitical context of late 18th century India. Like From the Holy Mountain, it also examines the interactions of Christianity and Islam, emphasizing the surprisingly porous relationship between the two in pre-modern times. At the heart of White Mughals is the story of a love affair which saw a British dignitary, the East India Company resident of Hyderabad, Captain James Achilles Kirkpatrick, convert to Islam and marry Khair-un-Nissa, a Hyderabadi noblewoman of royal Persian descent. As the British resident of Hyderabad, Kirkpatrick is shown to balance the requirements of his employers, the East India Company, with his sympathetic attitude to the Nizam of Hyderabad. The very title of White Mughals indicates its subject: the late 18th- and early 19th-century period in India, where there had been ‘a succession of unexpected and unplanned minglings of peoples and cultures and ideas’. On one level, the book tells the tragic love story of James Kirkpatrick, ‘the thoroughly orientalised’ British Resident in Hyderabad and Khair, a beautiful young Muslim noblewoman. On another level, the story is about trade, military and political dealings, based on Dalrymple’s researches among letters, diaries, reports, and dispatches (much of it in cipher). Out of these sources he draws a fascinating picture of sexual attitudes and social etiquette, finding an ‘increasingly racist and dismissive attitude’ among the British ruling class towards mixed race offspring, after the rise of Evangelical Christianity. He paces the gradual revelations with a novelist’s skills, leading us on, after the death of Kirkpatrick, to ‘the saddest and most tragic part of the whole story’. The doomed lovers actually engender an optimistic coda, when their two children move to England. Jacen Solo, now the Sith lord Darth Caedus, presses on with his mission to "bring order" to the galaxy by seizing control. As he sinks deeper into the dark side of the Force, he grows ever less hesitant to sacrifice anyone—family, friends, even allies—to achieve his ends. By the novel’s close, nearly all who once stood by him have turned against him, including his secret lover Tenel Ka and almost every Jedi. The only remaining ally appears to be Tahiri Veila, whom he manipulates through the memory of his dead brother, and her partner, Anakin Solo.

This story marks a turning point in Caedus’ descent into Sith power. In the prior novel, he had already sent a warrant to arrest his own parents, Leia and Han Solo. Now, he becomes more willing to commit atrocities—targeting civilian centers and forests on Kashyyyk—without hesitation. He no longer hesitates to sacrifice even close kin for his ambitions. He begins to relish the fear his subordinates feel. In one instance, he orders the arrest and execution of a spy who was in danger of being uncovered and killed by the Corellian government, using the act as a warning to others not to return to the Galactic Alliance if their cover was compromised.

The novel also shows the steady collapse of Caedus’ personal relationships as he wages war across the galaxy. He sends troops to seize the Jedi Praxeum on Ossus and then orders the deaths of all adult Jedi there—including his twin sister, Jaina—aiming to secure control over the younger trainees. Though this effort ultimately fails, both sides suffer severe casualties.

He manipulates Tenel Ka into surrendering her last fleet, leaving her and their daughter vulnerable to a coup—only after she realizes how far he has gone does she withdraw her support. He also convinces his cousin, Ben, to assassinate the deposed Chief of State, Cal Omas, then warns Coruscant authorities of an impending attack, setting up the murder as a trap. When Ben is later unwilling to carry out the deed, Caedus tortures him in a bid to force him into becoming a Sith apprentice. The plan is interrupted when Luke Skywalker arrives and intervenes, leading to a fierce lightsaber duel. Luke spares Jacen only when he sees that Ben is still at risk of falling to the dark side.

A separate thread in the novel uncovers a hidden network of Sith on Korriban and reveals new details about Ship, the ancient Sith vessel Ben had recovered from Ziost.

text:
A terrestrial laser scanner is a fast, high-precision device used increasingly in forest inventory research. In this study, we designed and implemented an automated, low-cost terrestrial laser scanner using a SICK LMS-511 two-dimensional laser scanning sensor and a stepper motor. The system, named BEE (developed by the Department of Electronic Engineering, Beijing Forestry University), captures three-dimensional data of forest trees. The BEE scanner and its supporting software are specifically tailored for forest inventory applications. The software enables smooth control of the scanner and facilitates the acquisition of angular, range, and intensity data. These data are then processed into point clouds, range maps, and intensity maps.

Using the point cloud data, trees were detected from a single scan slice within each plot, and a local ground plane was fitted for each detected tree. The specific software then automatically estimated diameter at breast height (DBH), tree height, and tree position. Experiments were conducted in an artificial ginkgo forest in Haidian District, Beijing. Four 10 m × 10 m square plots were selected. The BEE scanner collected single-scan data from each plot, and the resulting DBH, tree height, and tree position estimates were analyzed. Manual measurements were also collected in the same plots for comparison.

The trunk detection rate across all four plots was 92.75%. The root mean square error (RMSE) for DBH estimation was 1.27 cm, and for tree height estimation, it was 0.24 m. Tree position estimates aligned closely with actual ground-truth positions. The scanner was also tested in a more natural forest setting at JiuFeng Forest Park. Two 5-meter-radius plots were scanned. In the plot with flat terrain, eleven trees were successfully detected and DBHs estimated. However, tree detection failed in the second plot due to undulating ground conditions.

Results demonstrate that the BEE scanner can efficiently estimate key structural parameters of plantation trees. It shows strong potential for practical use in forest inventory, particularly in uniformly structured, flat-terrain settings. The system’s affordability, automation, and accuracy suggest it could support scalable and repeatable forest monitoring efforts.

text:
Surgical education videos traditionally employ a single fixed viewpoint, which may limit the information available during complex procedures. To address this, we developed a multiple point-of-view (POV) video system and evaluated its effectiveness compared to conventional single-POV training. Eight cameras captured a hip resurfacing procedure performed by an expert attending surgeon in the operating theatre. Thirty medical students were randomly and equally assigned to the multiple-POV group (experimental group [EG]) or the single-POV group (control group [CG]). All participants practiced inserting a pin into the femoral head as demonstrated in their respective video. Pin insertion trajectories were measured and compared to the pre-operative surgical plan to assess angular deviation and entry point accuracy. Two orthopedic attendings evaluated performance using a modified global rating scale (GRS). Participants completed a pre-video knowledge test and a post-simulation assessment, along with a Likert-scale questionnaire.

The EG demonstrated a 29% reduction in angular deviation compared to the CG (p = 0.037), with no significant difference in entry point distance (p = 0.204). GRS scores were 3.5% higher in the EG (p = 0.046). Post-intervention knowledge scores increased by 32% in the EG compared to the CG (p < 0.001), and Likert-scale scores improved by 21% (p = 0.002). Pre-video knowledge scores did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.721).

The multiple POV video system yielded measurable improvements in technical accuracy and self-reported learning outcomes, indicating enhanced effectiveness for training in hip surgery.

text: Continuing investment in a failing plan, commonly referred to as the sunk-cost fallacy, reflects a persistent deviation from rational decision-making. Resources previously committed cannot be recovered, and thus economic theory asserts that decisions ought to be based solely on anticipated future outcomes. Empirical research indicates that this fallacy arises from negative affect, though prior studies have primarily examined incidental emotional states unrelated to the decision context. This study investigates whether the sunk-cost fallacy is instead driven by integral affect—emotions directly elicited by the decision scenario itself. Study 1 established a positive association between integral affective reactions and the tendency to continue investing in failing plans. Study 2 replicated this finding using a within-subjects design, demonstrating that the type of scenario (invest vs. non-invest) fully mediates the sunk-cost effect through integral affect. The mediation effect was specific to emotional responses tied to the scenario, not to unrelated incidental affect. Study 3 replicated these results and further revealed that the relationship between affect and the sunk-cost fallacy is moderated by justification: participants who provided a justification for their initial decision exhibited greater resistance to the fallacy and reported lower levels of negative affect in response to the scenarios. Study 4 tested the role of cognitive processing by imposing cognitive load to reduce conscious deliberation and increase reliance on affective intuition. Under high cognitive load, the association between integral affect and the sunk-cost fallacy strengthened significantly compared to low-load conditions. These findings indicate that integral emotional responses, not incidental affect, underlie the sunk-cost fallacy, and that deliberate justification and cognitive capacity modulate its strength. The results suggest that interventions aimed at promoting justification and reducing affective impulsivity may help mitigate this pervasive decision-making bias.

Continuing investing in a failing plan (i.e., the sunk-cost fallacy) is a common error that people are inclined to make when making decisions. It is impossible to get resources back that already have been invested. Hence, economic theory implies that decision makers’ decisions should only be guided by future gains and losses. According to the literature, the sunk-cost fallacy is driven by negative affect. Previous studies focused on negative incidental affect. We investigated, in contrast, whether the sunk-cost fallacy is caused by integral affect elicited by the specific decision context. Study 1 demonstrated a positive relationship between affective reaction and the sunk-cost fallacy. Study 2 replicated the finding in Study 1 in a within-subjects design, and demonstrated a full mediation of type of scenario (invest vs. non-invest) on the sunk-cost effect, mediated by integral affective reaction. A mediation using a within-subjects design additionally demonstrated that the effect is mediated by integral emotional responses experienced in relation to each scenario, and not by incidental emotional states that are unrelated to the scenarios. Study 3 replicated findings in the previous studies, and demonstrated that the relation between the sunk-cost fallacy and affect is moderated by justification. Participants who justified their decision were more resistant to the sunk-cost fallacy, and showed less negative affect elicited by the scenarios, than participants who did not justify their decision. Study 4 provided supporting evidence for our hypothesis by hindering conscious deliberation, and promoting reliance on affect, via cognitive load. The results showed that the relation between affect and the sunk-cost fallacy was stronger for participants under high cognitive load, than under low-load. The paper discussed how this research leads to new ways to protect against the sunk-cost fallacy in the discussion.
</source>

On Saturday night in Houston, Texas, police discovered eight people dead inside a home, including six children. Around 9:00 p.m. local time, deputies from the Harris County Sheriff's Office responded to a welfare check at the residence. After multiple attempts to contact someone inside, officers forced entry. David Conley, 49, was arrested and charged with the murders. Authorities reported that Conley had a history of violent behavior and had previously been imprisoned on multiple occasions. His most recent arrest occurred just a month prior, when he was accused of striking his girlfriend’s head against a refrigerator in the same house. At the time of the killings, he was also wanted on an assault charge involving a family member.

The victims’ names and ages were released on Sunday: Valerie Jackson, 40; her husband Dwayne Jackson, 50; their children Nathaniel Jackson, 13; Honesty Jackson, 11; Dwayne Jackson Jr., 10; Caleb Jackson, 9; Trinity Jackson, 7; and Jonah Jackson, 6. Conley was the biological father of Nathaniel Jackson. Investigators say he told them he had once lived with Valerie Jackson and claimed he broke into the home after she changed the locks.

On Tuesday, Conley spoke to reporters from an administrative segregation unit at the Harris County Jail. He stated he had been living in the house and had promised to move out, but had nowhere else to go. He said he was upset when he returned to find the locks had been changed. He also claimed that all the victims had disrespected and mistreated him. When asked about his son Nate by KPRC reporter Robert Arnold, Conley said he would not discuss the events inside the home, as his lawyer had advised against it. He did, however, offer a brief statement about the Jackson children.

text: A subset of children experiencing jealousy in friendships exhibit adaptive responses such as problem solving and communication when outsiders disrupt their bonds; however, others disengage from the relationship or engage in retaliation toward peers. Individual differences in these reactions may be explained by children’s beliefs about the malleability of social traits. Drawing on learned helplessness theory and developmental research on implicit personality, this study tested whether children endorsing high entity beliefs—regarding social characteristics as fixed and social outcomes as uncontrollable—would be more likely than those with growth-oriented views to favor asocial or antisocial responses to outsider interference, particularly when attributing blame internally versus externally. Two hundred eighty-six sixth- through eighth-grade students, mostly Caucasian, participated in an experimental assessment of these predictions. While hypothesized interactions between entity beliefs and locus of blame were not observed, children who viewed social traits as changeable reported greater perceived control over the situation in internal attribution conditions compared to those who believed traits were unchangeable. Additionally, children with pessimistic dispositions were more inclined to endorse asocial and antisocial behaviors and less likely to support prosocial alternatives than their optimistic peers. Findings suggest that both implicit beliefs about social traits and dispositional optimism significantly influence how children navigate social jealousy.

text:
The novel is set in Comala, a town in the Mexican state of Colima. It opens with Juan Preciado, who promises his mother on her deathbed that he will return to Comala to find his father, Pedro Páramo. He claims he did not plan to keep this promise until he begins experiencing vivid, subjective visions of her. His narration is disjointed, alternating between his present journey and fragmented dialogue from the life of his father, who lived during a time when Comala was still a thriving community, not the desolate ghost town it has become.

Juan moves through Comala, encountering residents who appear to him as dead. Midway through the story, Juan dies. After this point, the narrative shifts almost entirely to the time of Pedro Páramo. The characters Juan encounters—Dolores Preciado, Eduviges Dyada, Abundio Martínez, Susana San Juan, and Damiana Cisneros—are now described through an omniscient voice, less filtered by personal perception.

Two narrative perspectives emerge: one rooted in Juan’s fragmented, spectral experience, and another offering a more objective account of events under Pedro Páramo’s rule. This omniscient narration details Pedro’s life from youth to death—his early infatuation with Susana San Juan, his rise to power, his violent control over the town, his pattern of sexual relationships, and his eventual decline. He is cruel and emotionally detached. Though he raises one of his illegitimate sons, Miguel Páramo, whose mother dies in childbirth, he does not form a bond with him. He does not love his father, who died when Pedro was a child, nor either of his two wives.

His only enduring emotional attachment is to Susana San Juan, a childhood friend who leaves Comala with her father as a girl. He fixates on her return, dedicating his life to winning her, believing she is the one person who could redeem him. When she returns, he takes her as his wife, but she remains emotionally distant, mourning her dead husband Florencio. She spends much of her time sleeping and dreaming of him.

After her death, the church bells toll without pause, and the townspeople celebrate as if it were a festival. Pedro buries his only true love, then turns on the town, furious at its indifference. As the most powerful figure in Comala, he withdraws from all activity. The town ceases to function. Without his direction, farms fail, supplies vanish. People starve. This is why, in Juan’s account, Comala appears as a dry, lifeless place—its vitality destroyed not by time, but by one man’s refusal to sustain it.

text:
Zahi Hawass, Egypt’s leading archaeologist and Secretary General of the Supreme Council of Antiquities, has announced the discovery of a rare white marble statue believed to depict Alexander the Great. The find was made during a Greek excavation in Alexandria, led by Calliope Papacosta. Hawass also noted that satellite imagery has identified numerous archaeological sites that may contain buried monuments.

Egypt’s Culture Minister, Farouk Hosni, is backing efforts to protect these sites, having introduced laws that restrict illegal digging in areas confirmed to hold historical remains. The National Authority for Remote Sensing, Space Sciences (NARRS), in collaboration with Mubarak City for Scientific Research (MuCSAT), used satellite data, aerial photography, and ground laser scanning to locate 132 previously unexcavated sites. Among them are a site north of Lake Qarun in the Faiyum region and another in the city of Habu.

The Egyptian Ministry of Tourism is now dispatching archaeologists to these areas ahead of construction projects, aiming to safeguard priceless historical artifacts. At the Faiyum site near Cairo, excavations have already turned up items from multiple eras, including a leather-stitching awl, fishing gear, weapons, jewelry, pottery, coins, sawfish remains, whale fossils, and a block dating to 3150 BCE that depicts one of two kings named Scorpion.

Elsewhere, Iran is preparing to move its three salt mummies—discovered in the Chehrabad Salt Mine in 1993—to a climate-controlled vacuum display in Zanjan. These mummies, known as Salt Men, date from the Parthian period (237 BCE–224 CE) to the Sassanid era (224–651 CE), and will be better preserved in the new facility.

text: In mountainous regions of China, coal mining-induced ground subsidence and surface cracking represent significant geological hazards that threaten both infrastructure and ecological stability. This study focuses on the village of Nanyetou in Shanxi Province, where damage to residential buildings was linked to the extraction activities of the 15110 working face at the Baiyangling coal mine. Field investigations identified active surface cracks and structural damage to homes, prompting a detailed assessment of the underlying mechanisms. Using established mining subsidence principles and boundary angle theory, the extent of surface influence from underground mining was mapped. However, conventional subsidence models failed to fully account for the observed building damage, particularly in complex terrain. To address this gap, the study applied slope stability analysis, calculating the slope safety factor before and after mining using the Janbu method. Results indicated a notable reduction in slope stability following mining operations, with decreased safety factors directly correlating to the observed structural damage. This decline was attributed to altered stress conditions and potential loss of shear strength in the slope materials due to subsurface extraction. Field observations and InSAR-derived displacement data provided independent confirmation of the instability and its link to mining activity. The findings underscore that in mountainous mining zones, building damage cannot be reliably predicted through subsidence models alone. Instead, a geomechanical approach considering slope stability is essential for accurate risk assessment. These insights offer a practical framework for evaluating building vulnerability in similar geological and mining contexts, supporting more effective mitigation strategies in regions where coal extraction and human settlements coexist.

Ground subsidence and surface cracks caused by coal mining are typical man-made geological hazards that can severely damage the ecological environment and buildings. In China, within the theme of sustained and stable development, accurate assessment of mining-related building damage is paramount in order to address the contradiction between coal mining enterprises and building owners. Previous research in China focused mainly on the mining areas of plains, and only a few studies have considered building damage caused by intensive mining in mountainous areas. First, based on field investigation, this study located ground surface cracks and assessed the damage to buildings in the village of Nanyetou in Shanxi Province (China) attributable to the exploitation of the 15110 working face of the Baiyangling coal mine. Second, based on the mining subsidence law and boundary angle, the surface influenced boundary caused by underground mining was determined. However, as the existing subsidence theory cannot adequately explain the phenomenon of building damage, the damage was investigated from the perspective of slope stability analysis, and the slope safety factor before and after working face mining were calculated using the Janbu method. The analytical results showed that slope instability due to a decrease of the safety factor because of the coal mining activity was the principal reason for damage to the village buildings, a finding that was confirmed by field survey and InSAR monitoring displacement. The results of this study could provide guidance and reference for the assessment of building damage caused by underground mining in mountain areas.
</source>

text: The Swallows plan to sail the Goblin to Hamford Water and camp with their father, but he is summoned for naval duties at the last moment. Left behind, he maroons them on a small island, leaving them with a rough outline map of the surrounding waters—the area they name Secret Water—and urging them to chart it before he returns. Unbeknownst to them, he has arranged for the Amazons to arrive from the Lake District, coming by dinghy to join them. Soon after landing, the children discover strange footprints in the mud, which they fear might be from some wild creature. The prints turn out to belong to the Mastodon, a local boy who mistakes them for the Eels, a family who regularly camp in the region. When the Eels finally arrive, they are initially hostile, but soon settle into a friendly rivalry. Though war-related distractions and shifting tides prevent them from finishing the chart on time, the two groups—each unaware the other had started—complete separate drafts of it early on the final morning.

text: Cadel Piggot is brought to a psychologist at a young age because he is unlike other children—too sharp, too fast with machines, too far ahead in understanding. His mind operates in ways that confound peers and adults alike, and while his brilliance offers power, it carries a cost: his actions, however unintentional, unravel the lives around him. He does not yet grasp the weight of his intellect, nor how easily it might be used to harm. His path is shaped by figures who claim to guide him, but whose motives are hidden. Phineas Darkkon, said to be his father, looms as a shadow of intellect and malice. Thaddeus Roth, the psychologist, is later revealed to be Prosper English, a known associate of Darkkon and a man who also asserts he is Cadel’s father. At the Axis Institute, a school built for exceptional minds, Cadel trains in IT and hacking—skills he uses without moral instruction. The world he shapes through code becomes unstable, unravelling relationships and environments. Then, a quiet presence enters his life: a girl named Sonja Pirvert, who moves through life with cerebral palsy, though Cadel does not know her name or condition at first. It is through her that he begins to understand restraint, consequence, and something like compassion—just in time to stop himself from becoming what he was meant to be.

text:
A novel multiple point-of-view (POV) video system was developed to address limitations in current surgical education videos, which rely on a fixed single POV that may inadequately convey spatial relationships during complex procedures. Eight cameras were used to record a hip resurfacing procedure performed by an expert attending surgeon. Thirty medical students were randomly assigned to either the multiple POV group (experimental group [EG]) or the single POV group (control group [CG]). Participants completed a pre-video knowledge test, viewed their assigned video, then performed a simulated pin insertion into the femoral head, guided by the video demonstration. Post-simulation, a repeat knowledge test and a Likert-scale questionnaire were administered.

Objective performance was assessed by comparing the pin insertion trajectory with the pre-operative plan. Angular deviation was 29% lower in EG compared to CG (p = 0.037), with no significant difference in entry point distance (p = 0.204). Two orthopedic attendings evaluated performance using a modified global rating scale (GRS); EG scores were 3.5% higher than CG (p = 0.046). Knowledge test scores increased by 32% in EG versus CG (p < 0.001), and Likert-scale responses improved by 21% (p = 0.002). No significant difference in pre-video knowledge test scores was observed between groups (p = 0.721).

The results indicate that the multiple POV video system improves accuracy in trajectory planning and enhances self-reported and expert-validated performance in surgical skill acquisition for hip resurfacing compared to single POV. The findings support the use of multi-perspective video in surgical education to improve technical learning outcomes.

text: Aging is linked to increased fall risk, with diminished capacity to recover balance following postural perturbations representing a key contributing factor. This impairment is likely attributable to age-related declines in lower limb strength. The present study examined the influence of age-related strength loss on non-stepping balance recovery during quiet standing, without restricting movement to the ankle, as in prior investigations. Two experiments were performed. In the first, five young adults (20–30 years) and six older adults (70–80 years, community-dwelling) recovered balance without stepping from a backward displacement of the support surface. Balance recovery capability was assessed as the maximum backward platform displacement tolerated. The older group exhibited a 27% reduction in maximal platform displacement (11.8±2.1 cm) compared to the young group (16.2±2.6 cm). In the second experiment, forward dynamic simulations using a two-segment, rigid-body model explored the effects of altering strength in hip extensors/flexors and ankle plantar flexors/dorsiflexors under typical age-related strength reductions. The model predicted diminished maximal platform displacements exclusively when plantar flexion and hip flexion strength were reduced. These findings confirm previously documented age-related reductions in balance recovery ability and underscore the critical role of plantar flexor strength in maintaining postural stability following perturbation.

text: This study evaluated an online intervention grounded in health literate design and behavior change theory to reduce unhealthy snacking, addressing a gap in health literacy guidance that emphasizes education over actionable tools. Four hundred forty participants were recruited via online platforms and randomized to one of three conditions: (1) a health-literate action plan involving guided implementation intentions; (2) a standard action plan using self-guided implementation intentions; or (3) an education control condition featuring a healthy snacking fact-sheet. The primary outcome was self-reported frequency of unhealthy snacking, assessed at one-month follow-up. Of the initial cohort, 373 participants (84.8%) completed follow-up. Health literacy was measured using the Newest Vital Sign (NVS); 52% of participants had adequate health literacy, while 24% had low and 25% had possibly low health literacy. At follow-up, lower health literacy was significantly associated with higher unhealthy snacking frequency. Although no overall group differences were observed, a significant interaction emerged between health literacy level and intervention type (b = 1.7, p = 0.03). Among participants scoring 2 points below the NVS mean (M = 3.4, SD = 2.0), the health-literate action plan was associated with 8 fewer weekly servings of unhealthy snacks compared to the standard action plan. Conversely, those scoring 2 points above the mean reported 6 more servings of unhealthy snacks when using the health-literate action plan. These results indicate that a one-size-fits-all approach to health information may not optimize behavior change, and that tailoring intervention components to individual health literacy levels may enhance effectiveness, particularly for those with lower health literacy. ANZCTR identifier: ACTRN12617001194358.

text: Intonation plays a critical role in speech perception, contributing significantly to speech recognition across languages. This study examines whether intonation cues influence the unmasking of Mandarin Chinese speech in noisy environments. Intelligibility of multi-tone Mandarin sentences was assessed under three intonation conditions—flattened, typical, and exaggerated—using either two-talker babble or steady-state noise as maskers. Unlike most prior investigations, this experiment isolates intonation by preserving tone information while manipulating only the fundamental frequency (F0) contour. Results demonstrate that recognition of final keywords was consistently higher under the original F0 contour compared to flattened or exaggerated F0 contours, regardless of masker type. Moreover, exaggerated intonation reduced intelligibility more severely under speech maskers than under noise maskers. These findings indicate that unnatural intonation impairs comprehension of tone-language speech—even when lexical tones are intact—and that such distortions particularly hinder speech recovery in complex, multi-talker acoustic environments. The data suggest that prosodic integrity is essential for effective communication in real-world listening scenarios, especially in competing talker situations.

text: Although some jealous children respond to outsider interference in friendships through problem solving or discussion, others withdraw from the relationship or retaliate against friends or third parties. These findings suggest that beliefs about social stability and dispositional affect play meaningful roles in shaping responses to social jealousy, even in the absence of expected interaction effects.

text: A terrestrial laser scanner offers rapid, high-precision data collection and has seen increasing use in forest inventory research. This study presents an automated, low-cost terrestrial laser scanner, designated BEE (developed by the Department of Electronic Engineering, Beijing Forestry University), built around a SICK LMS-511 two-dimensional laser scanning sensor and a stepper motor. The BEE scanner is designed specifically for three-dimensional scanning of forest trees and is paired with customized software to manage operations and collect data, including angular measurements, range readings, and intensity values. The collected data are processed into point clouds, range maps, and intensity maps. Using point cloud data from a single scan per plot, trees were detected, and a local ground plane was fitted for each detected individual. From these, the diameter at breast height (DBH), tree height, and tree position were estimated automatically via the integrated software. The BEE scanner was tested in an artificial ginkgo forest located in Haidian District, Beijing, using four 10 m × 10 m square plots. Single-scan data were collected from each plot. Manual measurements were also taken for comparison. Tree trunk detection achieved a rate of 92.75% across all plots. The root mean square error (RMSE) for DBH estimation was 1.27 cm, and for tree height, it was 0.24 m. Tree position estimates closely matched actual locations. The scanner was further tested in a more natural setting at JiuFeng Forest Park, where two 5-meter-radius plots were scanned. In the plot with flat terrain, eleven trees were successfully detected and DBH estimated. However, in the plot with undulating ground, tree detection failed. Results demonstrate that the BEE scanner can reliably estimate structural parameters of plantation trees and holds strong promise for practical use in forest inventory applications.

text: Ground subsidence and surface cracking from coal mining represent common human-induced geological hazards, capable of significantly compromising both the ecological environment and structural integrity of buildings. In China, where sustained and stable development remains a priority, accurately assessing mining-related building damage is critical to resolving tensions between coal operations and affected communities. While prior studies in China have largely centered on flatland mining regions, few have examined building damage resulting from intensive mining in mountainous terrain. This study begins with field surveys to identify surface cracks and evaluate building damage in Nanyetou Village, Shanxi Province, linked to extraction from the 15110 working face at the Baiyangling coal mine. Next, using established mining subsidence principles and boundary angle models, the surface influence zone caused by underground mining was mapped. However, because conventional subsidence theory falls short in fully explaining observed building damage, the analysis shifted to slope stability. The Janbu method was applied to calculate the slope safety factor both before and after mining activity. Results revealed that mining-induced reductions in slope stability—driven by declining safety factors—were the primary cause of structural damage in the village. This conclusion was supported by field observations and displacement data from InSAR monitoring. These findings offer valuable insight for evaluating building damage from underground mining in mountainous regions, providing a foundation for more reliable risk assessments and mitigation planning.

text:
The Eastern Conference defeated the Western Conference in the 2008 National Basketball Association All-Star Game, held at the New Orleans Arena in New Orleans, Louisiana. The final score was 134-128 in favor of the East. The West trailed by 13 points at the start of the fourth quarter, but mounted a comeback fueled by New Orleans point guard Chris Paul, who recorded seven assists during the period. With 2:48 remaining, Brandon Roy scored a layup off an assist from Paul, giving the West a 122-119 lead—the largest lead they achieved in the game.

The East responded with two three-pointers from Ray Allen. Chris Paul then tied the game with a three-pointer of his own. After that, the East reasserted control with a layup from Dwyane Wade, another three-pointer from Allen, and a driving dunk from LeBron James. With 8.7 seconds left, Brandon Roy made a three-pointer that reduced the deficit to three points, but Ray Allen made three free throws to secure the victory for the East.

The All-Star Game was the centerpiece of the weekend’s events, but the festivities included several other competitions highlighting player talent. In the Rookie Challenge, the Sophomores defeated the Rookies 136-109. Cleveland Cavaliers guard Daniel Gibson was named MVP, scoring all 33 of his points from three-pointers. His performance broke Kyle Korver’s 2005 record of seven three-pointers in a single game. The Sophomores extended their winning streak to six consecutive victories.

Team San Antonio claimed victory in the Three-Point Shootout, defeating Team Chicago in the final round. The squad included San Antonio Spurs forward Tim Duncan, former Spurs center David Robinson, and Silver Stars guard Becky Hammon. The win came on a halfcourt shot made by Duncan.

Deron Williams won the Playstation Skills Challenge with a record time of 25.5 seconds in the final round. His performance surpassed that of Chris Paul, who recorded 31.2 seconds. Dwyane Wade, who had won the event in each of the previous two years, was eliminated in the first round with a time of 53.9 seconds. Jason Kidd also failed to advance, finishing the course in 39.7 seconds.

Toronto Raptors guard Jason Kapono won the Three-Point Shootout for the second consecutive year, becoming the first player to achieve back-to-back victories since Peja Stojakovic in 2002 and 2003. Kapono tied the record of 25 points in the final round, previously set by Mark Price and Craig Hodges in 1986. Other finalists included Daniel Gibson, who scored 17 points in the final round, and Dirk Nowitzki, the 2006 champion, who scored 14. Peja Stojakovic, Richard Hamilton, and Steve Nash were eliminated in the first round.

The West trailed by 13 at the beginning of the fourth quarter, but rallied behind New Orleans point guard Chris Paul, who had seven assists in the final period. With 2:48 remaining, Brandon Roy scored a layup on an assist from Paul, giving the West a 122-119 lead, their biggest lead of the game.

The East then answered back with two three-pointers from Ray Allen, before Chris Paul tied the game with a three-pointer of his own. However, the East would then take the lead and the game with layups from Dwyane Wade and Allen, as well as a driving dunk from LeBron James. A Brandon Roy three-pointer put the game within three points with 8.7 seconds left, but 3 free throws from Ray Allen sealed the win for the East.

Although the All-Star game itself is the highlight of the All-Star festivities, the weekend would not be complete without the league's best players showing their skills in other events, including the Rookie Challenge, Three-Point Shootout, and the fan-favorite Slam Dunk Contest.

The Sophomores defeated the Rookies 136-109 in this game featuring the best young players in the league. Cleveland Cavaliers guard Daniel Gibson was named the game's MVP, with all 33 of his points coming from 3 point shots. He broke Kyle Korver's Rookie Challenge record of seven three-pointers, set in 2005. This was the sixth straight victory for the Sophomores.

text:
It is August 1949 in Ndotsheni, a village in the South African countryside near Ixopo. The Rev. Stephen Kumalo, the Black priest of St. Mark’s Church, receives word from his brother John, who lives in Johannesburg, that his sister is in distress. Moved by concern, Stephen resolves to journey to the city not only to assist her but also to find his son Absalom, who has been working in the gold mines. Upon arrival in Johannesburg, he learns his sister will not leave her circumstances but asks him to care for her young son, Alex. After some searching, Stephen reunites with Absalom, who has recently been released from jail. Absalom confides that he and his friends plan to commit a robbery, driven by desperation to avoid a life in the mines. His pregnant girlfriend, Irina, pleads with him to reconsider, but he proceeds. During the robbery, Absalom fatally shoots Arthur Jarvis, a white man and a close friend of Stephen’s.  

As Absalom is taken into custody, Stephen is overwhelmed by grief and uncertainty. He struggles to reconcile the truth of his son’s actions with his faith, wondering how he will tell his wife, Grace, and questioning whether he still believes in God ("Lost in the Stars"). He prays: “O Tixo, Tixo, Help Me.” At trial, Absalom’s two accomplices lie under oath and are acquitted, but Absalom, overcome by remorse, speaks the truth and is sentenced to death. Stephen performs a wedding ceremony for Absalom and Irina in prison, then returns to Ndotsheni with Irina and Alex. In the village, Alex and the infant son of Arthur Jarvis begin to form a quiet friendship, a fragile bond between two families bound by tragedy.  

Back in Ndotsheni, Stephen announces he can no longer serve as minister. His congregation, too, feels the weight of his departure, their faith now strained. On the morning of the execution, the air is still and dark. Stephen waits alone, listening to the clock. At four o’clock, the father of the murdered man arrives. He speaks not in anger, but in sorrow, acknowledging that he, too, has lost a son. In that moment, despite their different races and the loss that has torn them apart, he extends a hand in friendship. Stephen accepts it.

Authorities in Brisbane, Australia, have detained a 27-year-old man linked to the failed bombing attempts in Glasgow and London, which occurred on June 29 and June 30. The individual, identified as Mohammed Haneef, was apprehended at Brisbane International Airport yesterday evening at 11:00 p.m. AEST (UTC+10). He is not an Australian citizen and is originally from India.

He is one of eight suspects arrested in connection with the London and Glasgow attacks, six of whom are either practicing physicians or studying medicine. The UK’s terror threat level remains at critical, signaling that a further attack could occur at any time, prompting heightened security along major transit networks.

In response to ongoing concerns, a controlled explosion was carried out earlier today on a suspicious package found outside Hammersmith Station on the London Underground. The incident caused the temporary closure of Hammersmith and Barons Court stations for one hour. Tower Hill and East Ham stations were also briefly shut under similar circumstances. All four stations have since reopened, and police operations continue across the affected areas.

text:
Five teenagers—Olivia, Mo, Charlie, Stella, and Wen—end up in detention for separate reasons. While waiting, they hear a jingle on the radio and begin singing along. The experience leads them to form a band. Initial disagreements over musical direction fade as they begin to trust one another. They decide to perform at the school’s Halloween Bash, but face opposition from fans of Mudslide Crush, a popular band. Ray, a member of Mudslide Crush and a school bully, targets Olivia, mocking her for the band. Mo, Charlie, and Stella intervene. In response, Stella spits lemonade into Ray’s face. He calls her “lemonade mouth,” and the name sticks. They adopt “Lemonade Mouth” as their band name.

Before the Bash, the school removes the lemonade machine that inspired their name, as part of a sponsorship deal with a sports drink company for a new gym. The band feels betrayed and vows to challenge the decision. At the performance, students are surprised by their music, which features trumpets and ukuleles. Their sound is unconventional, but the audience responds.

The band members grow close through shared hardship. After Olivia’s cat dies, they gather at her house to support her. In private conversations, they reveal personal struggles: Stella believes she is unintelligent and struggles with her parents; Wen worries about his father’s upcoming marriage to a 26-year-old woman; Mo, an immigrant from India, feels alienated at school; Charlie shares that his twin brother died at birth. Olivia confesses that her parents had a teenage pregnancy, and her mother abandoned her father, who raised her alone until he was convicted of armed robbery and manslaughter.

Charlie develops feelings for Mo, who reciprocates. The band gains traction, appearing on the radio and performing at a local restaurant. Their success is short-lived. Just before the annual battle of the bands, their equipment fails: Stella’s ukulele breaks, Wen injures his lip, Charlie burns his hand, Olivia loses her voice, and Mo becomes ill. These setbacks prevent them from performing well in the competition.

Despite the poor result, fans sing along to their songs, offering solidarity. Afterward, Charlie and Mo kiss and begin dating. Stella reconciles with her parents and learns she has a learning disability. Wen gives Olivia a new kitten, and they grow close.

text: Men who have sex with men (MSM) in Japan bear a disproportionate burden of HIV, representing 78% of all male HIV cases reported in 2016. Each year, over 30% of newly diagnosed HIV infections in Japan are identified at the AIDS stage, indicating a substantial proportion of individuals remain unaware of their infection status. An estimated two-thirds of Japanese MSM are not connected to the gay community, and prior research has predominantly relied on samples drawn from gay venues, potentially missing a large segment of the population. This study assessed HIV testing prevalence and associated factors among MSM in Greater Tokyo who use gay mobile geo-social networking applications—platforms shown to improve access to MSM who are not reached through traditional venue-based surveys. A sample of 1,657 MSM was recruited via advertisements on these apps. Lifetime HIV testing prevalence was 72.8%, and testing within the past six months was 29.7%. In multivariable regression models, higher lifetime testing was linked to older age, higher education, greater HIV knowledge, and engaging in anal intercourse with both regular and casual male partners. Attendance at gay venues also predicted higher testing rates. Conversely, testing was lower among those who consistently use condoms with a regular male partner, those who are married, those living outside central Tokyo, and those who have both male and female sexual partners. These findings indicate that MSM who use gay mobile apps in Greater Tokyo do not meet Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommendations for annual HIV testing among high-risk populations. Given limited HIV prevention funding, moderate lifetime and recent testing rates, and the widespread use of mobile apps among this group, leveraging popular gay mobile apps to promote nearby HIV testing services may offer a cost-effective strategy to reach non-community-attached MSM, particularly youth and individuals at elevated risk for rapid progression to AIDS.

text:
A Spanish civil guard was killed and another seriously wounded in Capbreton, on France’s southwest coast, in a shootout with suspected members of the Basque separatist group ETA.

The incident occurred around 8:30 a.m. UTC, as the two plainclothes officers were returning to their vehicle after leaving a local coffee shop. They were ambushed by two men who opened fire. Agent Raul Centeno Pallón died at the scene; his colleague, Fernando Trapero Blázquez, sustained critical injuries and remains in a coma.

The civil guards were engaged in a joint surveillance operation with French police targeting ETA activity in southern France. They had apparently been spotted and identified by the suspects. Following the attack, the two men and a woman fled in a car. After traveling approximately 70 kilometers, the suspects abandoned the vehicle and stole another, seizing the driver. The hijacked driver was kidnapped, placed in the trunk, and later found bound to a tree.

This marks the first fatality attributed to ETA since it resumed hostilities in June, though the group has continued carrying out numerous non-lethal attacks.

The incident follows a day in which Spain’s National High Court issued arrest warrants for 46 of 52 Basque nationals previously prosecuted and sentenced on charges of supporting ETA’s separatist ideology.

text: Intonation plays a critical role in speech perception, contributing to segmental and supra-segmental processing in spoken language. This study examined the influence of intonation on the intelligibility of multi-tone Mandarin Chinese sentences under conditions of competing auditory maskers. Three intonation conditions—flattened, typical, and exaggerated—were applied while preserving lexical tone contours, isolating the effect of pitch contour variation. Intelligibility was assessed using sentence recognition performance in the presence of either two-talker babble or steady-state noise. Results indicated that recognition of final keywords was significantly higher under the original fundamental frequency (F0) contour compared to both decreased and exaggerated F0 contours, regardless of masker type. Notably, the exaggerated F0 contour produced greater degradation in intelligibility under two-talker speech maskers than under steady-state noise, suggesting that non-linguistic pitch patterns disrupt speech segregation in complex auditory scenes. These findings demonstrate that even when lexical tone is intact, unnatural intonation contours impair the ability to unmask speech from background interference, particularly in environments with competing voices. The results underscore the functional importance of natural prosodic patterns in tone languages, highlighting that accurate intonation supports speech perception not only in the absence of noise but also in challenging listening conditions.

This study aims to investigate whether intonation cues affect the unmasking of Mandarin Chinese speech in the presence of interfering sounds. text:
Flemington Racecourse in Melbourne hosted the 147th running of the Melbourne Cup today. The race covered 3200 meters, and the New Zealand-bred horse Efficient won in a time of 3:23.24. This marked the first time since Phar Lap, another New Zealand horse, that a horse has won the Cup in consecutive years. Efficient had previously won the 2006 Victorian Derby.

The finish was dramatic. Michael Rodd, riding Efficient, overtook Purple Moon in the final stretch. Purple Moon placed second; Mahler finished third. Mahler had led at the 1600-meter mark but faded in the closing stages. Tungsten Strike, the early leader, came in 21st (last). The odds for Efficient were 24-1 to win and A$7.40 for a place.

This victory is the third Melbourne Cup win for owner Lloyd Williams, who previously won in the 1980s. Williams entered two horses in the race: Efficient and Zipping. Zipping finished fourth. Nick Williams, Lloyd’s son, was present at the track and had high expectations for Efficient. The horse had been a favorite in the 2006 Cup but was scratched before the race.

text: In *The Celestine Prophecy*, one of the main characters vanishes during a solo journey through the Appalachian Mountains, leaving behind a thread of mystery that mirrors the book’s deeper themes. The story unfolds as a kind of spiritual quest, exploring ideas about parallel dimensions, past lives, and the journey from conception through death to an afterlife. It presents a vision of human destiny shaped by inner choices, where fear about the future—especially the looming possibility of a dictator, or Antichrist, rising and not being defeated—threatens to derail Earth’s spiritual awakening. The characters experience these ideas not as abstract theory but as lived reality, deeply felt and real to them. Central to the narrative is the belief that every soul belongs to a larger "Soul Group," a collective of beings united by a shared purpose in the evolution of the cosmos. At times, one soul from the group incarnates into physical life, making deliberate choices about its circumstances, while the others remain in a state of observation. Each soul shapes its reality through intention, and the consequences of those choices manifest as both earthly experience and the nature of life after death. These consequences aren’t random—they reflect the soul’s decisions. To resist the fear-driven narrative of apocalypse and failure, the protagonists hold firmly to a hopeful, Utopian "World Vision," refusing to entertain its opposite, until that vision ultimately overpowers the fear at the story’s climax.

<source>
 One of the characters of The Celestine Prophecy disappears while exploring a forest in the Appalachian Mountains. The book discusses ideas about other dimensions, past lives, conception and birth, the passage through death to an afterlife, hell and heaven. It also illustrates the author's vision of human destiny and the notion that fear of the future is endangering Earth's spiritual renaissance. In the story, each individual soul is part of a larger "Soul Group", which shares the mission of helping the evolution of the cosmos. At times, a soul from a given Group incarnates itself, choosing the conditions of its life according to its needs, while the other souls observe. Each soul creates a reality around itself, which later brings consequences upon it. These consequences take the form of life and afterlife, which vary according to the person's choices. On Earth, people speak of the prophecy written in the Book of Revelation as if it were coming true. Many fear that it will come partly true, in that a dictator (an Antichrist) will arise, but will not be thrown down. To counteract this idea, which is damaging to the spiritual renaissance, the protagonists hold their own, Utopian "World Vision" to the exclusion of its opposite, until it dominates the opposite at the book's climax. All of these ideas are experienced as if real by the characters.
</source>

text:
Guidance addressing health literacy typically emphasizes health education over actionable tools, despite the importance of behavior for self-management. This study evaluated an online intervention grounded in health literate design principles and behavior change theory, aiming to reduce unhealthy snacking. Four hundred forty participants were recruited online and randomized to one of three conditions: 1) Health-literate action plan (guided implementation intention); 2) Standard action plan (self-guided implementation intention); 3) Education (healthy snacking fact-sheet). The primary outcome was self-reported unhealthy snacking, assessed at one-month follow-up.

Of the 440 participants, 373 (84.8%) completed follow-up. Half the sample had adequate health literacy (52%); the other half had low (24%) or possibly low (25%) health literacy, as measured by the Newest Vital Sign (NVS). At follow-up, lower health literacy was associated with higher levels of unhealthy snacking, and no overall difference was observed across intervention groups. However, a significant interaction emerged: participants with lower health literacy reported less unhealthy snacking when using the health-literate action plan compared to the standard action plan, while those with higher health literacy reported more snacking under the same condition (b = 1.7, p = 0.03). Specifically, individuals scoring two points below the mean NVS (M = 3.4, SD = 2.0) who used the health-literate action plan consumed 8 fewer serves of unhealthy snacks, whereas those scoring two points above the mean consumed 6 more serves using the same tool.

These findings suggest that a universal precautions approach to health information may be insufficient for promoting action, and that tailoring interventions to health literacy level could enhance effectiveness. ANZCTR identifier: ACTRN12617001194358.

text:
A Spanish civil guard was killed and another seriously injured in a shooting attack in Capbreton, a town on France’s southwest coast, late this morning. The incident occurred around 8:30 a.m. UTC, when two plainclothes officers were entering their vehicle after leaving a coffee shop. They were ambushed by two men who opened fire. Raul Centeno Pallón died at the scene, while Fernando Trapero Blázquez sustained critical injuries and remains in a coma.

The officers were engaged in a joint surveillance operation with French law enforcement targeting members of the Basque separatist group ETA. Authorities believe the suspects identified the two Spanish guards during their patrol and carried out the attack in retaliation. Following the shooting, the two men and a woman who was with them fled in a vehicle. After traveling approximately 70 kilometers, the suspects abandoned their initial car and stole another, during which they kidnapped the driver, placed him in the trunk, and later left him tied to a tree.

This marks the first fatality attributed to ETA since it resumed hostilities in June, despite having carried out numerous attacks that did not result in death. The incident occurred the day after Spain’s National High Court issued arrest warrants for 46 of 52 Basque nationals previously prosecuted and convicted for supporting ETA’s separatist objectives.

text:
Mohsin Musa Matawalli Atwah, 45, accused of being an Al-Qaeda explosives expert, was killed in a missile strike on Wednesday night in Pakistan, according to Sheikh Rashid Ahmed, Pakistan’s information minister. At least eight other individuals believed to be associated with terrorist networks, including both foreign nationals and Pakistani citizens, were also killed. The identities of these individuals have not been confirmed. At least two children are believed to have died in the attack.

Atwah, also known as Abdul Rahman Al-Muhajir, Muhammad K.A., and Abdel Rahman, is accused of orchestrating the August 7, 1998 bombings of the U.S. embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam. Those attacks killed 20 Americans and at least 200 Africans. He remains on the FBI’s list of most wanted terrorists, with a $5 million reward for information leading to his capture.

The strike occurred in Naghar Kalai, a village in North Waziristan near the Afghanistan border. Pakistani forces conducted the operation using missiles and explosives fired from assault helicopters. Authorities believe that associates of the deceased may have removed and buried the bodies in an unknown location. However, at least four local tribesmen who died in the strike were buried in the town’s cemetery.

The U.S. FBI and U.S. officials in Egypt have not confirmed Atwah’s death.

text: Palestinian officials reported on Sunday that Egypt had temporarily reopened the Rafah border crossing to permit a limited number of pilgrims from the Gaza Strip to travel to Mecca for the Islamic pilgrimage. The move coincided with the start of Ramadan, a significant period in the Islamic calendar. The Rafah crossing remains the sole official entry point between Gaza’s 1.7 million residents and Egypt. Officials stated that 800 pilgrims were scheduled to cross on Sunday, while approximately 15,000 Palestinians from Gaza waited to enter Egypt, including some holding foreign passports. About 4,000 of those waiting seek medical treatment abroad. Since the ousting of Egyptian President Mohamed Morsi in July 2013, Egypt’s military authorities have imposed stringent restrictions on the border, frequently closing it for extended periods. These closures have intensified pressure on Gaza’s population. Egyptian officials assert that Hamas has launched terror attacks into Egypt and interfered in domestic affairs, claims the group denies.

text:
It is August 1949 in the South African village of Ndotsheni, known as “The Hills of Ixopo.” The black priest of St. Mark’s Church, the Rev. Stephen Kumalo, receives a letter from his brother, John Kumalo, who lives in Johannesburg, warning that his sister is in trouble. Determined to help her and to find his son Absalom, who works in the mines, Stephen sets out for the city. In Johannesburg, he learns his sister will not leave, but she asks him to care for her young son, Alex. After much searching, he finds Absalom, who has recently been released from jail. Absalom, now in the company of friends, plans to steal in order to earn enough money and escape a future in the gold mines. His pregnant girlfriend, Irina, pleads with him not to go, but he proceeds, despite her warnings.

During the robbery, Absalom shoots and kills Arthur Jarvis, a white man and a close friend of his father, Stephen. As Absalom is sentenced to hang, Stephen wrestles with how to tell his wife, Grace, and begins to face a crisis of faith. He wonders whether his son should lie to save his life or speak the truth and face death. In prayer, he calls out, “O Tixo, Tixo, help me.” At trial, Absalom’s two friends lie under oath and are released, but Absalom, truly remorseful, tells the truth and is condemned to die.

Stephen performs a wedding ceremony for Absalom and Irina while he is imprisoned. He then returns to Ndotsheni with Irina and Alex. The boy, Alex, and the child of Arthur Jarvis begin to play together, slowly forming a bond. Upon his return, Stephen tells his congregation he can no longer serve as their minister, and their faith, too, is shaken.

On the still-dark morning of the execution, Stephen waits alone as the clock approaches four o’clock. Unexpectedly, the father of the murdered man arrives. He speaks of the shared loss of a son. In recognition of their mutual grief, and despite the vast divide of race, he offers friendship. Stephen accepts.

text:
The story opens when a young Cadel Piggot is brought to a psychologist, marked as different—too sharp for his age, too fast with computers. His brilliance is not just cleverness but a force, shaping events beyond his control. As he uses his mind to navigate systems and outthink others, the consequences ripple outward, unraveling the lives around him. He is not yet aware, but his intellect carries weight that no child should bear. 

The turning point comes through a quiet connection with a girl named Sonja Pirvert, who has cerebral palsy—though he doesn’t know her name or condition at first. It is through her presence, fragile and steady, that a moral anchor takes hold, not through grand revelation, but through quiet consistency. 

His path is further entangled by Phineas Darkkon, a man presented as his father—evil, brilliant, and cold. Equally deceptive is Thaddeus Roth, his psychologist, who is in fact Prosper English, a known criminal and Darkkon’s lieutenant. Roth claims paternity too, deepening the confusion. 

Cadel is sent to the Axis Institute, a school built for him, a place of twisted purpose cloaked in academic veneer. There, he meets others like him—prodigies shaped by design, trained in IT and hacking to become tools of control. His talent is not his own, but a weapon forged in deception. And yet, something in him resists the script.
